title: Resistivity and Conductivity: Ω·m, Ω·cmil/ft, S/m, %IACS
h1: Resistivity and conductivity — Ω·m, %IACS and S/m
description: Copper is 1.72 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m = 100% IACS. Aluminium is 61% IACS. Silver is 106% IACS. Cable ampacity scales inversely.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Resistivity is the material property; resistance is the geometry-scaled result. Wire and PCB engineering never leave this equation.
body: Resistivity ρ and conductivity σ = 1/ρ describe how well a material carries current, independent of shape. Cable engineers, PCB designers and materials scientists each keep a different favourite unit.

> 1 Ω·m = 100 Ω·cm = 10⁶ µΩ·cm
> 1 Ω·cmil/ft = 1.662 × 10⁻⁹ Ω·m
> %IACS = 100 × (σ_material / σ_annealed_copper), σ_Cu = 5.8001 × 10⁷ S/m
Silver: 1.59 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m (106% IACS). Copper: 1.68–1.72 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m (100% IACS). Aluminium: 2.65 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m (61% IACS). Steel: 15 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m. Nichrome: 110 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m.

1000 A bus bar, 10 m long, aluminium (2.65 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m). Cross-section 500 mm². R = ρL/A = 2.65 × 10⁻⁸ × 10 / 5 × 10⁻⁴ = 530 µΩ. Voltage drop V = IR = 0.53 V. Same bar in copper: 0.34 V. IACS immediately shows the ratio (61%): copper drop = aluminium drop × 0.61.
%IACS is the cleanest cross-metal comparison. Convert to Ω·m for actual resistance.

faqs.a: Yes — copper's temperature coefficient is +0.393 %/K. Aluminium is +0.403 %/K. Hot conductors carry less current.
Resistivity divided by thickness, in Ω/sq (ohms per square) — a shape-independent metric for thin films.
